On title, see Introduction. Alluding to some event in his history, as in <reference osisRef="1Sam.23.13">1Sa 23:13</reference>, the Psalmist avows his confidence in God, when admonished to flee from his raging persecutors, whose destruction of the usual foundations of safety rendered all his efforts useless. The grounds of his confidence are God's supreme dominion, His watchful care of His people, His hatred to the wicked and judgments on them, and His love for righteousness and the righteous.</title> <div sID="gen8440" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5559"/><hi type="bold">1. my soul--</hi>me (<reference osisRef="Ps.3.2">Psa 3:2</reference>).<div eID="gen8440" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8441" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Flee--</hi>literally, "flee ye"; that is, he and his companion.<div eID="gen8441" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8442" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as a bird to your mountain--</hi>having as such no safety but in flight (compare <reference osisRef="1Sam.26.20">1Sa 26:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lam.3.52">La 3:52</reference>). <div eID="gen8442" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 11 Psa 11:1-7 . On title, see Introduction. Alluding to some event in his history, as in 1Sa 23:13 , the Psalmist avows his confidence in God, when admonished to flee from his raging persecutors, whose destruction of the usual foundations of safety rendered all his efforts useless. The grounds of his confidence are God's supreme dominion, His watchful care of His people, His hatred to the wicked and judgments on them, and His love for righteousness and the righteous. 1. my soul-- me ( Psa 3:2 ). Flee-- literally, "flee ye"; that is, he and his companion. as a bird to your mountain-- having as such no safety but in flight (compare 1Sa 26:20 ; La 3:52 ).

Literally, "The foundations (that is, of good order and law) will be destroyed, what has the righteous done (to sustain them)?" All his efforts have failed. <div eID="gen8444" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5562"/><div sID="gen8445" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5562"/><hi type="bold">4. temple ... heaven--</hi>The connection seems to denote God's heavenly residence; the term used is taken from the place of His visible earthly abode (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.6">Psa 2:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.3.4">3:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Cor.5.7">5:7</reference>). Thence He inspects men with close scrutiny. <div eID="gen8445" type="x-p"/>

Their punishment is described by vivid figures denoting abundant, sudden, furious, and utter destruction (compare <reference osisRef="Gen.19.24">Ge 19:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.18.15">Job 18:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.7.15">Psa 7:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.9.15">9:15</reference>).<div eID="gen8447" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8448" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">cup--</hi>is a frequent figure for God's favor or wrath (<reference osisRef="Ps.16.5">Psa 16:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.23.5">23:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.20.22">Mt 20:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.20.23">23</reference>). <div eID="gen8448" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 6. Their punishment is described by vivid figures denoting abundant, sudden, furious, and utter destruction (compare Ge 19:24 ; Job 18:15 ; Psa 7:15 ; 9:15 ). cup-- is a frequent figure for God's favor or wrath ( Psa 16:5 ; 23:5 ; Mt 20:22 , 23 ).
entries.reader_content_plain: 6. Their punishment is described by vivid figures denoting abundant, sudden, furious, and utter destruction (compare Ge 19:24 ; Job 18:15 ; Psa 7:15 ; 9:15 ). cup-- is a frequent figure for God's favor or wrath ( Psa 16:5 ; 23:5 ; Mt 20:22 , 23 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5565"/><div sID="gen8449" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5565"/><hi type="bold">7. his countenance--</hi>literally, "their faces," a use of the plural applied to God, as in <reference osisRef="Gen.1.26">Ge 1:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.22">3:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.11.7">11:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.6.8">Is 6:8</reference>, &c., denoting the fulness of His perfections, or more probably originating in a reference to the trinity of persons. "Faces" is used as "eyes" (<reference osisRef="Ps.11.4">Psa 11:4</reference>), expressing here God's complacency towards the upright (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.34.15">Psa 34:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.34.16">16</reference>). <chapter eID="Ps.11"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. his countenance-- literally, "their faces," a use of the plural applied to God, as in Ge 1:26 ; 3:22 ; 11:7 ; Is 6:8 , &c., denoting the fulness of His perfections, or more probably originating in a reference to the trinity of persons. "Faces" is used as "eyes" ( Psa 11:4 ), expressing here God's complacency towards the upright (compare Psa 34:15 , 16 ).
